the E. coli pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase complex is composed of three subunits, and that these are the pyruvate-oxidizing subunit (Pox), the flavoprotein subunit (Fp), and the ferredoxin subunit (Fds).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular structure of the pyruvate decarboxylase of Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of the E. coli pyruvate oxidoreductase complex, which consists of the following three components: pyruvate decarboxylase, lipoic acid-containing dihydrolipoyl transacetylase, and dihydrolipoprotein reductase.

the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of the E.coli PDH complex and its individual subunits, with the aim of understanding the molecular basis for the regulation and control of this key enzyme complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pyruvate oxidoreductase of E. coli is composed of three distinct polypeptides, two of which (the E1 and E2 subunits) are identical to those of the pyruvatedehydrogenase complex of animal sources, while the third (E3) is a new polypeptide.

the E. coli pyruvate oxidoreductase complex is a multienzyme complex consisting of the following subunits: pyruvate decarboxylase (EC 4.1.1.1), dihydrolipoyl transacetylase (EC 2.3.1.12), and dihydrolipopoyl dehydrogenase (EC 1.8.1.4).
there is a single polypeptide of molecular weight 80 000, with a single cysteine residue in the active site, which catalyzes the transacetylation of dihydrolipoyllysine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we were able to show that the pyruvate oxidoreductase complex from E. coli is a hetero-octamer composed of two dihydrolipoyl transacetylase, two dihydridrolipoyl dehydrogenase, two dihydroxyacid dehydrogenase and two lipoate acetyltransferase subunits.
the pyruvate oxidoreductase system of Escherichia Coli is a complex of at least four enzymes.

the pyruvate oxidase reaction is catalyzed by an enzyme complex consisting of three different components, pyruvate decarboxylase (EC 4.1.1.1), dihydro-lipoamide dehydrogenase (EC 1.6.4.3) and dihydro-lipo-amide acetyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.12).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pyruvate kinase gene ( pykF ) is essential for the growth of E. coli K12.
the pyruvate kinase and pyruvate decarboxylase genes are not essential for the growth of the yeast on glucose, but they are necessary for growth on pyruvate.
the pyruvate kinase gene is not required for the formation of the pyruvatedehydrogenase complex.
